description: We’re a passionate team building Astrominoes, an interactive space-mission simulator that turns real NASA mission trade-offs into gameplay. We’re interested in space science, AI, simulation, and game development, with skills in software engineering, UI/UX, and problem-solving. We’re looking for teammates skilled in astronomy/physics, AI/ML, frontend/game development, UI/UX, or storytelling/presentation.
summary:
Astrominoes is an intricate aerospace simulation engineered for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, meticulously designed to encapsulate the multifaceted complexities of celestial mission architecture.

Thrust into the pivotal role of a NASA Mission Director, players navigate a rigorously crafted four-phase odyssey. The journey begins with the structural synthesis in the Assembly Bay, demands the calculated precision of Orbital Trajectory Injection, requires the arduous oversight of Deep Space Telemetry, and culminates in a comprehensive Mission Debrief. Participants must deftly orchestrate critical engineering trade-offs—harmonizing payload mass, budgetary constraints, communication latency, and power generation (via solar arrays or radioisotope thermoelectric generators)—across three progressively formidable campaigns targeting the Lunar South Pole, Europa, and the interstellar medium.

The simulation distinguishes itself through an uncompromising adherence to authentic astrophysics.
details:
Designing an actual space mission involves competing trade-offs that students and enthusiasts rarely get to experience hands-on: payload mass vs. rocket capacity, power generation (Solar vs. RTG) vs. solar distance (1/r2), communication bandwidth vs. speed-of-light latency, and budget vs. scientific return.

Astrominoes puts players in the commander's seat of a NASA Mission Directorate across 4 authentic phases:

  1. Assembly Bay (Phase 1): Balance wet mass, electrical buses, propulsion systems, and scientific sensors under strict physics and budgetary limits. Features the A.D.A.M. (Aerospace Diagnostic & Advisory Mentor) AI Copilot, 1-Click Loadout presets, and 1-Click Auto-Balance for accessible gameplay.
  2. Orbital Trajectory Injection (Phase 2): Execute a timed trans-injection thruster burn to break Earth orbit into a Hohmann transfer ellipse, with optional gravitational slingshots and A.D.A.M. Flight Assist.
  3. Deep Space Telemetry (Phase 3): Manage real-time flight telemetry (speed-of-light radio delay, solar flux drop-off, power shunt buses) with Warp Speed controls (1×, 2×, 4×) and resolve critical in-flight anomalies (solar flares, micrometeorite strikes, reaction wheel drift).
  4. Mission Debrief (Phase 4): Review complete mission ratings (Grade S/A/B/C), science collected (GB), and archive telemetry records to the global leaderboard.

NASA Data Attribution & Science Citations

This game models authentic astrophysics equations and real mission parameters derived from official NASA databases:

  • NASA JPL Horizons System: Celestial gravitational parameters, planetary ephemerides, and delta-$v$ transfer vectors.
  • NASA Planetary Data System (PDS): Radiation environment maps, solar irradiance drop-off models (1/r2), and planetary atmospheric boundaries.
  • NASA Open Data Portal (data.nasa.gov): Subsystem hardware masses, ESPA-class payload adapters, and RTG power degradation profiles.
  • Tsiolkovsky Rocket Equation: Δv=Isp⋅g0⋅ln⁡(m0mf)
  • Inverse-Square Law for Solar Flux: S(r)=S0r2where S0=1361 W/m2

Framework: Next.js 16 (App Router, Turbopack)

UI Library: React 19

Styling: Tailwind CSS v4 with custom aerospace HUD glassmorphism

3D Graphics: Three.js with GLTF models

Icons: Lucide React

Database: MongoDB / Mongoose with in-memory fallback

Audio: Native Web Audio API procedural synthesis
